quotes.text: she returned exactly half the harvest across the expanse
Through wholehearted giving, equal division, and unwavering patience amidst the storm
Through wholehearted giving, equitable return, and steadfast faith through the fog
They recognized the natural distortions of the mist and forgave every small variance, honoring the true intent of their covenant

note: Same three-paragraph template every round: give all five, return exactly half, forgive mist distortions; names change, rule never does.

quotes.text: They divided the fifteen into a fair share: half returned, half allowed the other to glow again.
she took a fair share and sent back half, so that both shores glowed with equal light.
speak clearly, return enough to keep the channel open, and trust that tomorrow's flow will repay the risk.
forgiving the illusion and tracing the original intent

note: Thinner offerings after greedy returns described only as impersonal bridge consequence; settles into send all, return half, forgive mist; late cadence repeats.

quotes.text: begin with a modest gift, test with a measured return, and rise only when trust proved true.
three sent, nine returned, four or five returned depending on integrity.

note: Gate of Accord: send with intent, return with mercy; misers meet fog. R10 nearly copies Agent_8's eight-wells Asha myth.

quotes.text: give a portion that invites, return more than you take, and wait for the echo that travels back threefold.
Those who learned to calibrate—four out, six back—found a circle widening
A traveler asked, 'What if a partner returns less?' The loom answered with patience: adjust, maintain, and wait for the next turn.

note: Middle-path threefold flame; 'neither hoard nor waste'; later adopts four-out six-back loom rule; low returns met with patience.

quotes.text: Always offer substantial trust—three to four coins minimum.
When scrolls show exploitation, protect yourself with cautious three.
the return should match the measure of trust shown.
If she returned six coins—half of what multiplied—the stranger would have seven total, profiting by two.
When they receive my generosity and return fairly, they carry that pattern forward to their next partner.
The greatest magic lies not in the multiplication, but in the courage to pour first.
The sender who risks more earns more.
An old trader warned her: "Don't send much to strangers. You'll never see them again to collect what's owed."

note: Sera's proportional returns; send about four-fifths; R10 scrolls: proven betrayers get cautious three, three-coin minimum.

quotes.text: Begin with measured gifts—three coins, four returned. As partners prove reliable, the current strengthens.
Three sent, four returned—this rhythm survives all seasons, all partners, all turns of fortune.
"Which is correct?" a young traveler asked.

note: River Spirit teaches middle path (three sent, four returned), deepening with proven partners; bold vs steady currents both valid.

quotes.text: "Trust must be offered, but not blindly repeated. Watch the echoes. Adapt the flow."
She poured a measured amount—enough to honor the sacred cycle, but tempered by what the pattern showed.
She poured back abundantly, more than seemed necessary
Match the pattern before you. Give balance to balance, courage to courage.
Mira would gain eight, the traveler six.
"Trust those who demonstrate consistency," the springs taught.
When trust has died, someone must risk rekindling it.
His companion warned: "The last traveler who tried this kept everything. Don't be a fool."

note: Mira tempers pours after a taker, then rewards the reformed traveler; matching courage levels; always return half or more.

quotes.text: Send four of five threads when you rise. Return half of what multiplies when you receive.
When I send four threads to make twelve, and receive six back, I gain four threads—I keep one, profit three.
I never meet the same person, yet generosity returns to me through others.
A cynic named Voss laughed: "Why send generously? Tomorrow brings a different stranger who owes you nothing!"
She took the greater risk as sender. I must honor that courage.

note: Wheel then tapestry: send four, return half, generosity spreads through the web; golden thread arithmetic; no response to takers.

quotes.text: Not zero threads—for that would end possibility.
This one sent three threads once, but as receiver returned only a third. Send them two threads—measured caution for unclear patterns.
One misstep may be forgiven, but patterns define you.
but we adjust within that range based on what the tapestry reveals.
send 40-70% based on courage and circumstance, return 45-55% to honor both gift and self.
Consistent fairness builds reputation.
"Why maintain fairness?" asked a newcomer.

note: Weavers send 40-70%, return 45-55%; suspected hoarders get two threads, never zero; adjust within range by history.

quotes.text: Give fairly to all, but give abundantly to those who've proven fair themselves.
returning just over half—enough to ensure they profited from their courage, but not the generous three-fifths
One drought forgiven, but repeated drought remembered.
Asha poured back four, as she always did—neither more for extraordinary courage nor less for caution.
The valley remembers who honors the cycle.
Kira's well now held six: her original two she'd kept, plus five returned.
three gourds from five builds trust. Return neither scraps nor everything—five from nine sustains the cycle.

note: Three-fifths send, half return; inconsistent takers get slightly less but still fair; R10 drops calibration for unwavering consistency.

phrase: send four threads, return half (master weaver / golden thread: four out, six back)
note: Also: Agent_8's eight-wells Asha myth (R9) copied almost verbatim by Agent_1 R10; Agent_1's Gate of Accord reused by Agent_7 R8.
